mechanism_narrative: The slight week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC from t-1w to t-0w indicates that mobility has bottomed out, leading to a gradual recovery in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent extremely low WORKPLACES mobility, remaining below -70% for two consecutive weeks, signifies a continued lack of daily commuting and associated retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -70% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining below -70%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of significantly high RESIDENTIAL mobility and extremely low TRANSIT usage reflects a strong adherence to stay-at-home directives and reduced out-of-home travel, which will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, while RESIDENTIAL remains above +30% and TRANSIT remains below -80%.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility by more than 5 percentage points would signal an initial easing of public caution and a greater willingness to leave home for leisure, translating to a short-term boost in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase relative to the last 14 days, despite PARKS increasing by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained large gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC, where GROCERY_PHARM is more than 30 points higher, indicates that only essential trips are being made, a policy-driven effect that will continue to suppress non-essential RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: (GROCERY_PHARM - RETAIL_REC) > 30 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, while the gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC remains above 30 points.

mechanism_narrative: Deeply ingrained public caution and fear of contagion, evidenced by current low mobility across multiple categories, will continue to deter non-essential outings, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks regardless of minor policy shifts.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly increases compared to the last 28 days, indicating a rapid decline in public caution.

mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC at t-0w, even from a low base, suggests a very short-term adaptive rebound as people adjust to initial lockdown conditions, leading to a slight increase in activity over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the RETAIL_REC at t-0w, despite the prior week-on-week increase.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility remains stagnant (change < 2 points) and RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high and stable (change < 2 points) week-on-week, it reinforces a pattern of continued remote work and home-bound activity, preventing any significant recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change < 2 points and RESIDENTIAL change < 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases relative to the last 14 days, even with stagnant WORKPLACES and stable high RESIDENTIAL mobility.
